claims.content: The Customer Service Representative resolves a customer inquiry by handling the customer's complaints / concerns, accessing and editing customer information, researching bidding issues, and troubleshooting customer service issues.

goal.raw_text: The Customer Service Representative resolves a customer inquiry by handling the customer's complaints / concerns, accessing and editing customer information, researching bidding issues, and troubleshooting customer service issues.

claims.content: Customer Service Representative
The Customer Service Representative has access to the customer history page to aid in troubleshooting customer service issues.
The Customer Service Representative has user-level access with the permissions granted to access and edit customer information.
The customer can be searched by customer e-mail address, phone number, or customer name.
A customer contacts the call center with a complaint or concern that the Customer Service Representative must resolve.

trigger.raw_text: A customer contacts the call center with a complaint or concern that the Customer Service Representative must resolve.

claims.content: The Customer Service Representative accesses the Customer History page from the Administration Menu to aid in troubleshooting customer service issues.
The Customer Service Representative searches for the customer by customer e-mail address, phone number, or customer name.
The Results: section displays the customer's Last Name, First Name, City, ST, Zip, Phone, and E-mail address.
The Customer History page displays the Account Notes text box, a free-form text field for use by Customer Service representatives, and the Order History section.
The Customer Service Representative enters account notes in the free-form Account Notes text box.
The Customer Service Representative unlocks accounts in Review Status, as Review Status accounts can only be unlocked by a customer service representative.
If a customer account is deactivated, it will be listed in RED in the Results section.

If the Customer Service Representative needs to view Bid History, Order History, View Notes, or Reset Password, the Customer History page includes buttons for these functions that utilize anchor tags to take the user to the correct section further down the page.

If the Customer Service Representative deactivates a customer account, the system will require a supervisor's authorization code. A pop-up DIV layer will appear, asking for a supervisor's code. Only supervisors will know these codes, which will be issued by Administrators and generated by the Auction Admin application. Supervisors will not need to have Administrator access to input the codes.
If an Amazon Payments or PayPal customer has a history of non-payment whose auction orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days, the account will be subjected to an escalation process.

When an auction participant becomes subject to the escalation policy, they cannot bid again until a Customer Service Rep removes the account from Review Status. The only way for a customer to have their account removed from Review Status is by updating their account with a credit card. They may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%.

If a customer/bidder has unresolved (i.e., unpaid) auction winnings greater than 7 days old, the system automatically locks the account and puts the account into Review Status. The account in Review Status can only be unlocked by a customer service representative; the customer cannot unlock the account themselves by paying for the orders, because the orders are automatically cancelled after 7 days (168 hours). Exit: the Customer Service Representative unlocks the account.

If a customer has had orders cancelled, the Customer Service Representative can unlock their account if they haven't paid up to three times. Exit: the Customer Service Representative unlocks the account.

If a customer with unresolved (i.e., unpaid) auction winnings or a locked account contacts the call center, the Customer Service Representative simply reminds them that winning incurs an obligation to pay. Exit: the customer is reminded that winning incurs an obligation to pay.

Each time the seven day period passes and a order is cancelled, the Customer Service Representative will still need to remove the account from Review Status. If the customer wins and doesn't pay for a 56th auction, resulting in six unpaid orders, this puts the customer at 10.7% and subject to the escalation policy. Exit: the account is removed from Review Status; the customer is subject to the escalation policy if the threshold is reached.
The customer complaint/concern has been handled by the Customer Service Representative.
Customer information has been accessed and edited, bids have been removed in emergency circumstances only, and bidding issues have been researched.
The customer account has been edited and account notes have been entered in the free-form Account Notes text box.

If the account was in Review Status, the account has been removed from Review Status by the Customer Service Representative, because Review Status accounts can only be unlocked by a customer service representative.
If the customer had unpaid auction winnings, the customer has been reminded that winning incurs an obligation to pay.

If the account is subject to the escalation policy, the account has been removed from Review Status by the Customer Service Representative after the customer updated the account with a credit card, and the customer may not use PayPal or Amazon Payments again until their order cancel rate falls below 10%.
If the customer account is deactivated, the deactivation was approved by a supervisor's authorization code, and the deactivated account appears in RED.
